hypothesis: No individual numeric feature has a statistically significant linear correlation with performance_rating after multiple-testing correction.
rationale: The dataset is labeled pure_noise, suggesting features are independently generated. Any raw p < 0.05 correlations are likely false positives.
test_method: Pearson and Spearman correlation with Bonferroni and BH correction (CHK-05, CHK-15).

hypothesis: salary_band categories show no significant difference in mean performance_rating.
rationale: If features are noise, the categorical variable should also be unrelated to the target.
test_method: One-way ANOVA F-test (CHK-08) with Bonferroni adjustment.

hypothesis: A full OLS regression model has no predictive power beyond the intercept-only baseline.
rationale: Under the pure-noise assumption, the global F-test should fail to reject H0 and R² should be near zero.
test_method: OLS regression global F-test and R² (CHK-12); cross-validated RMSE comparison (CHK-14).
success_criteria: F-test p > 0.05 and cross-validated RMSE within 1% of baseline RMSE.

hypothesis: No feature achieves permutation importance significantly above zero in a random-forest model.
rationale: A non-linear model should also fail to find signal in pure noise data.
success_criteria: All feature importances have 95% CI overlapping zero.

rationale: Mean ≈ 50, std ≈ 10, and the 25th/75th percentiles are roughly symmetric around the median, consistent with normal generation.
test_method: Shapiro-Wilk test and histogram visual inspection (CHK-01).
success_criteria: Shapiro-Wilk p > 0.05 or visual confirmation of bell shape.

hypothesis: Predictor variables are mutually uncorrelated (no multicollinearity).
rationale: Independently generated features should have VIF values near 1 and low pairwise correlations.
success_criteria: All VIF values < 2 and all pairwise |r| < 0.15.
